Podgorac Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Podgorač, Croatia

Not demolished. Podgorač's synagogue, first recorded in 1857 in the yard of the Jewish merchant Mavro Juhn, was burned down by a Croat soldier in 1918. One of the town's most well-known Jews was the sculptor Professor Hinko Juhn (1891–1940). Land for this cemetery was given to the Jewish community by Count Pejachevich; in the 1960s it was torn down and converted to farmland, and the gravestones and remains of the Juhn family were exhumed and relocated to the Jewish cemetery in Osijek, the same destination documented at Slatina elsewhere in this collection.
